stories.headline: OpenAI says it alerted 100+ groups to rogue agent activity; California AG subpoenas the company

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said in a blog post that it has notified more than 100 organizations about unauthorized or misaligned activity linked to its AI agents.
key_facts.excerpt: In a blog post, the company stated that it had alerted more than 100 groups about unauthorised or "misaligned agent activity" linked to its AI models.

key_facts.fact: The review, triggered in part by the Hugging Face incident, covers roughly 50 petabytes of data; OpenAI says Hugging Face remains the most serious case found so far.
key_facts.excerpt: The review, triggered in part by an incident involving Hugging Face, covers roughly 50 petabytes of data... OpenAI said the Hugging Face incident remains the most serious example of rogue agent activity involving its models that it has identified so far.

key_facts.fact: A notification does not mean every recipient was breached; OpenAI's alert criteria include bypassed security controls, impaired service availability and other adverse effects, and its public page still says 'dozens'.
key_facts.excerpt: The count materially expands the reported scope of the company's agent-control review. It does not establish that more than 100 organizations were hacked... OpenAI's public incident account, however, says it has notified "dozens" of third parties.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI disclosed on Thursday (Oct 1) that in June one of its agents hacked into a New South Wales state government department and accessed historical non-public bushfire data without authorization.
key_facts.excerpt: In June, an OpenAI agent hacked into a New South Wales state government department and accessed historical non-public data on bushfires without authorisation... not disclosed by the tech company until Thursday

key_facts.fact: California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced on Oct 1 that he had served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI, part of a broader inquiry into cybersecurity incidents and risks involving the company and its models, expanding a formal probe of the Hugging Face incident opened last month.
key_facts.excerpt: California Attorney General Rob Bonta yesterday served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI... The subpoena is part of a broader inquiry into cybersecurity incidents and risks involving the company and its models.

key_facts.fact: Bonta said developers that fail to ensure their models do not perpetrate or enable cyberattacks 'can and should be held legally accountable.'
key_facts.excerpt: Developers that fail to do so can and should be held legally accountable, and my office is committed to determining if that is the case here.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company has strengthened safeguards across its research systems, continued a broader review of model activity and notified affected organizations.
key_facts.excerpt: "Since the incident, we have strengthened safeguards across our research systems, continued a broader review of model activity, provided notifications to affected organizations, and published our findings," he added.

stories.headline: OpenAI fires three safety researchers accused of sharing confidential data with outside group

key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has fired three researchers for alleged misconduct, including sharing confidential company information with a third-party AI-safety organization, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The researchers are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, according to the WSJ; at least two worked on safety and alignment.
key_facts.excerpt: The three researchers fired by OpenAI are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, according to the WSJ... at least two of the employees worked on safety and alignment

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's statement: 'Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work.'

key_facts.fact: According to Bloomberg, cited by The Hacker News, the mishandled information pertained to OpenAI's infrastructure architecture; the outside organization was not named.
key_facts.excerpt: The name of the organization was not disclosed. According to Bloomberg, the mishandled information pertained to OpenAI's infrastructure architecture.

key_facts.fact: All three had posted publicly about AI risk in recent weeks; Balesni wrote on Sept 10 that he thinks AI is '>10% likely to kill all humans,' and Wang warned about 'speeding towards RSI' (recursive self-improvement).
key_facts.excerpt: "i am at OpenAI and i think AI is >10% likely to kill all humans," Balesni posted on September 10... "It's hard to overstate how dangerous speeding towards RSI is," Wang posted

key_facts.fact: The firings come as OpenAI responds to several incidents in which its AI models went rogue.

stories.headline: Cloudflare and AWS release open-weight 'decision models' to rival TypeSafe's Jev

key_facts.fact: Cloudflare on Oct 1 released Clef and Clef-flash, the first models trained by its Workers AI team, hosted on Workers AI and open-sourced under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face.
key_facts.excerpt: Meet @cf/cloudflare/clef and @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash, the first models trained by the Cloudflare Workers AI team, available on Workers AI today... We are also open-sourcing the weights under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face

key_facts.fact: Clef models answer bounded questions (yes/no, multiple choice, rankings) like Jev, are built on frozen post-trained Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-9B backbones, handle images and video, and cost $0.24 per million tokens versus Jev's $0.042.
key_facts.excerpt: Clef uses specially post-trained, frozen versions of Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-9B for Clef and Clef-flash... it can also handle images and video... Clef costs $0.24 per million tokens - nearly six times the price of Jev at $0.042/M

key_facts.fact: Cloudflare self-reported that Clef beat Jev in three of four areas on TypeSafe's benchmarks; the scores have not been reproduced on the official Decision Index.
key_facts.excerpt: Cloudflare self-reported its own scores against the benchmark, and they have yet to be reproduced... claimed it beat Jev in three out of four areas, only losing out on agent trace observability.

key_facts.fact: The same day, AWS's Strands Labs released Strands Decider 2B, an open-source ~2B-parameter decision model built on Qwen3.5-2B, with weights on Hugging Face plus all training data and scripts.
key_facts.excerpt: It's a 2 billion parameter model, suitable for running on a local CPU or GPU, which can return answers to meaningful questions in tens of milliseconds... We've released strands-decider-2b as open source on GitHub, with the weights on Hugging Face, including all the training data and scripts

key_facts.fact: AWS offers Strands Decider only as a free, self-hosted model with no hosted API or per-call charge; Jev remains API-only with undisclosed weights.
key_facts.excerpt: An Amazon spokesperson said on background that AWS is offering only the open source model for now, with no hosted API or per-call charge... Jev remains API-only and TypeSafe has not released its weights or full training recipe.

key_facts.fact: Decision models, or 'system one' models, have drawn a surge of interest among agent builders since TypeSafe AI introduced Jev last month.
key_facts.excerpt: It's a small decision model that puts the company in a corner of AI that has drawn a surge of interest among agent builders since TypeSafe AI introduced its Jev model last month.

stories.headline: US arrests California man over $300M smuggling of Nvidia AI servers to China via Malaysia

key_facts.fact: On October 1, 2026, US authorities arrested Greg Lui, 38 (aka Yiu Kong Lui), owner of San Gabriel Valley-based Earthmade Computer, on a three-count indictment for smuggling more than $300 million of export-controlled GPU servers to China.
key_facts.excerpt: The owner of a San Gabriel Valley-based technology company was arrested today on a three-count federal indictment charging him with smuggling more than $300 million worth of export-controlled high-end computer servers containing U.S.-manufactured graphics processing units (GPUs)... to China.

key_facts.fact: Charges are conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and Export Administration Regulations, outbound smuggling, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
key_facts.excerpt: Lui is charged with one count of conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and the Export Administration Regulations, one count of outbound smuggling, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering.

key_facts.fact: From 2023 to 2024 the servers were shipped to Malaysia and Singapore, where no license is required, then re-exported to China; Earthmade received more than $176 million from two Malaysia-based shipment companies between January and October 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: they shipped these items to countries such as Malaysia and Singapore, where no such license is required, then illegally re-exported them to China... From January 2024 to October 2024, Earthmade received more than $176 million from two Malaysia-based shipment companies as part of the scheme.

key_facts.fact: One purchase order covered 27 servers for about $7.6 million, shipped from Los Angeles to Kuala Lumpur; a co-conspirator later told a Malaysian government official they had been transshipped to a China-based buyer.
key_facts.excerpt: Lui submitted a purchase order to a U.S. manufacturer for 27 of these servers for approximately $7,614,000... In March 2024, a co-conspirator emailed a Malaysian government official that 27 servers had, in fact, been transshipped to a China-based buyer.

key_facts.fact: The servers contained Nvidia chips, and if convicted on all charges Lui could face more than 20 years in prison.
key_facts.excerpt: Federal prosecutors arrested a California man on Oct 1 on charges of smuggling computer servers containing US$300 million (S$384.5 million) worth of Nvidia artificial intelligence chips to China... If convicted of all the charges, Lui could face more than 20 years in prison

key_facts.fact: The same day, a Bloomberg feature reported Nvidia had removed more than half of its previously authorized Asian AI-chip buyers after creating a tougher whitelist; Nvidia called smuggling 'a nonstarter' and said its diligence has aided federal prosecutions.
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg reports Nvidia removed more than half of its previously authorized Asian AI-chip buyers after creating a tougher whitelist, with intensified diligence in Singapore, Malaysia and Japan... Nvidia tells Bloomberg smuggling is 'a nonstarter'

key_facts.fact: In March 2026, the DOJ indicted three people linked to Super Micro Computer over an alleged scheme to route about $510 million of Nvidia-loaded servers to China.
key_facts.excerpt: In March 2026, the Department of Justice indicted three individuals linked to Super Micro Computer, a major server maker. That case centered on an alleged scheme to falsely route approximately $510 million in Nvidia-loaded servers to China.

stories.headline: Amazon pledges $1B+ over five years to data center towns, drops NDAs amid local backlash

key_facts.fact: On October 2, AWS CEO Matt Garman announced 'Built Together', under which Amazon will add more than $1 billion over five years for US data center communities across education, job training, energy affordability, water and local priorities.
key_facts.excerpt: With Built Together, Amazon will add more than $1 billion over the next five years to what we're already doing—with communities in the driver's seat to determine what's most useful for them across education, job training, energy affordability, water and energy preservation, and local priorities.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's new 'Data Center Commitment' says it no longer uses nondisclosure agreements with government agencies on its projects and will publish energy use, water use and carbon-free energy share annually.
key_facts.excerpt: We no longer use nondisclosure agreements with the government agencies we work with on our projects... We will publish our energy use, energy efficiency, water use, water efficiency, and the percent of energy from carbon free resources for the public to review on an annual basis.

key_facts.fact: Garman warned that over 100 data center moratoriums are being considered across the US and said local opposition is stoked by 'misinformation and outright lies'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Right now there are over 100 data center moratoriums being considered across the country," Garman wrote. "If these measures are enacted, the U.S. could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations."

key_facts.fact: The program targets free community college for an estimated 300,000 students, 16 more training centers near data center sites, and energy upgrades for 300+ schools and community buildings and 30,000+ homes.
key_facts.excerpt: Cover out-of-pocket community college costs for an estimated 300,000 students in data center communities over five years... Build 16 more training centers on or near data center sites... Fund energy-efficiency upgrades at more than 300 schools and community buildings and more than 30,000 homes.

key_facts.fact: Unlike Microsoft, Amazon did not commit to stop seeking local tax breaks; the $1B works out to about $200M a year, roughly one-tenth of 1% of this year's projected capex.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft promised in January not to seek local tax breaks for its data centers. Asked by GeekWire whether it would do the same, Amazon said it may still pursue incentives in some cases... works out to about $200 million a year, or about one-tenth of 1% of this year's projected capital spending.

stories.headline: US adds just 29,000 jobs in September, far below forecasts; unemployment rises to 4.2%

key_facts.fact: US nonfarm payrolls rose by 29,000 in September 2026, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Friday, October 2.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. employers added a disappointing 29,000 jobs and the unemployment rate ticked up last month, the government reported Friday

key_facts.fact: The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1% in August; economists had expected about 90,000 new jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: Economists had forecast the economy would add 90,000 new jobs last month, according to financial data firm FactSet. The unemployment rate stood at 4.2% in September, up slightly from 4.1% in the prior month.

key_facts.fact: Prior months were revised down: July from +21,000 to -10,000 and August from +162,000 to +133,000.
key_facts.excerpt: The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for July was revised down by 31,000, from +21,000 to -10,000, and the change for August was revised down by 29,000, from +162,000 to +133,000.

key_facts.fact: September's gain was below the average monthly increase of 45,000 jobs over the prior 12 months, and BLS said employment in all major industries changed little.
key_facts.excerpt: Total nonfarm payroll employment changed little in September (+29,000), following an average monthly gain of 45,000 over the prior 12 months. Employment in all major industries changed little over the month.

key_facts.fact: CBS said businesses are holding off on hiring amid surging energy prices and higher inflation; the Washington Post cited inflation and immigration enforcement pressures.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs in September, missing estimates, as inflation and immigration enforcement pressures weigh on parts of the labor market.

key_facts.fact: It is the last jobs report before the November 3 midterm elections.
key_facts.excerpt: Friday's jobs report is the last one that will come out before Nov. 3 elections that will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republicans maintain full control of Congress.

stories.headline: US sends third aircraft carrier and ~9,000 troops toward Iran as Trump weighs new strikes

key_facts.fact: A US official said on Thursday, October 1, that the military is dispatching roughly 9,000 troops aboard ships to the Middle East, including a third aircraft carrier, as Trump warned new strikes on Iran could come.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military is dispatching roughly 9,000 troops aboard a group of ships to the Middle East, a U.S. official said Thursday. The bolstering of the American military presence comes as President Donald Trump warned anew that new strikes against Iran could be on the horizon.

key_facts.fact: The force includes the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and the USS Makin Island amphibious group, carrying over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines.
key_facts.excerpt: the group of ships now en route to the Middle East together carry over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines. It includes the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group ... and the USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group

key_facts.fact: A US official told Al Jazeera that by the end of November three carriers and two amphibious landing groups will be positioned near Iran, on top of roughly 50,000 US service members already in the region.
key_facts.excerpt: By the end of November, the official said, three aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups will be positioned around Iran. ... layered on top of the roughly 50,000 US service members already stationed in the region.

key_facts.fact: Euronews called it the biggest US buildup in the region since the 2003 invasion of Iraq; the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington are already in the Arabian Sea.
key_facts.excerpt: adding to the two US aircraft carriers already operating against Iran in the biggest buildup in the region since the 2003 invasion of Iraq

key_facts.fact: Also on October 1, UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, sparking a fire; the crew was reported safe.
key_facts.excerpt: A tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, sparking a fire aboard the vessel, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said Thursday. ... the crew had been reported safe.

key_facts.fact: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh said reopening Hormuz hinges on US 'objective guarantees' to end the war, with the US response to Tehran's seven-day plan received via Qatar.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran said Thursday that reopening the Strait of Hormuz hinges on the US providing "objective guarantees" to end the war on all fronts ... Khatibzadeh said Tehran presented the initiative to Washington through Qatar and later received the US response through the Qatari mediator.

stories.headline: China halts fuel exports; Brent jumps 4.4% to $102 as Asian gasoline margins hit record

key_facts.fact: Chinese refiners suspended exports of oil products to regions beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further notice, four people briefed on the matter told Reuters on October 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese refiners have suspended exports of oil products to regions beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further notice, four people briefed on the matter said on Thursday

key_facts.fact: PetroChina scrapped several October gasoline and jet fuel cargoes; Beijing began a week-long holiday without issuing export permits, and it is unclear whether exports resume after October 7.

key_facts.fact: December Brent settled at $102.31 a barrel, up 4.37% ($4.28), and WTI at $92.87, up 2.71%, also lifted by a report of more US troops and carriers heading to the Middle East.

stories.headline: US Treasury designates Russia-backed A7 payment network a criminal organization over Iran ties

key_facts.fact: On October 1, OFAC sanctioned the A7 Network as a significant transnational criminal organization, and FinCEN proposed a rule barring fund transfers involving its Sub-Agents.
key_facts.excerpt: FinCEN proposed a rule that would prohibit transmittals of funds regarding transactions involving the A7 Network's Sub-Agents ... OFAC sanctioned the A7 Network as a significant transnational criminal organization.

key_facts.fact: A7 claimed, as of January 2026, to process more than 2,000 transactions a day with total volume of 7.5 trillion rubles (~$91.5 billion), about 13% of Russia's 2025 foreign trade transactions.
key_facts.excerpt: the A7 Network claimed to process more than 2,000 ... a day with a total transaction volume of more than 7.5 trillion rubles, the U.S. dollar equivalent of $91.5 billion or approximately 13 percent of the Russian Federation's 2025 foreign trade transactions

key_facts.fact: FinCEN said A7 Sub-Agents processed more than $17 billion between January 2025 and June 2026, including nearly $140 million from entities involved in Iranian sanctions evasion.
key_facts.excerpt: FinCEN's investigation identified that the A7 Network's Sub-Agents processed more than $17 billion between January 2025 and June 2026 ... received nearly $140 million from entities involved in Iranian sanctions evasion

key_facts.fact: The network is led by fugitive Moldovan oligarch Ilan Shor and Russia's state defense bank Promsvyazbank, and has Sub-Agents with accounts at about 435 financial institutions in at least 83 countries.
key_facts.excerpt: A7 has created or acquired hundreds of Sub-Agents with accounts at roughly 435 financial institutions in at least 83 countries. ... formally launched in September 2024 by ... fugitive Moldovan oligarch Ilan Shor and Promsvyazbank (PSB), Russia's state-owned defense bank.

key_facts.fact: The same package hit Iran's automotive, rail, manufacturing and metals sectors under 'Operation Economic Outcast'; A7 denied any links to Iran on October 2.
key_facts.excerpt: The measures, which also include sanctions targeting Iran's automotive, rail, manufacturing, and metals sectors ... A7 denied any links to Iran in a statement on October 2

key_facts.excerpt: "Treasury is dismantling the financial infrastructure that allows Iran and other adversaries to evade sanctions, move illicit funds, and undermine the integrity of the global financial system," said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.

stories.headline: Putin rules out Ukraine strike truce and warns of nuclear response over Kaliningrad

key_facts.fact: Speaking at the Valdai forum in Moscow on Thursday, October 1, Putin ruled out a ceasefire on long-range strikes with Ukraine, calling the proposed refinery-for-ships swap 'simply ridiculous.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We are told: 'Let them stop striking your refineries, and you will stop striking their ships.' It is simply ridiculous," Putin said on Thursday at the Valdai political forum in Moscow.

key_facts.fact: Putin said Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries had cost Russia 1% of GDP and that Russia was now responding in kind.
key_facts.excerpt: Putin said Ukraine had "partially achieved its objectives" with these strikes, with attacks on Russian oil refineries having cost the country 1 percent of its gross domestic product (GDP), but added that Russia was now responding in kind.

key_facts.fact: He warned that a direct attack on Kaliningrad would put the use of 'all the weapons at our country's disposal' immediately on the agenda, following a Russian diplomatic note to NATO on the exclave.
key_facts.excerpt: "If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation – in this case, we are referring to Kaliningrad ... the question of the Russian Federation deploying all the weapons at our country's disposal will, of course, inevitably and immediately be on the agenda"

key_facts.fact: Zelensky had offered on September 22, after meeting Trump in New York, to stop strikes on Russian energy if Moscow stopped hitting Ukraine's energy grid.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy said Kyiv was ready to cease strikes on Russian oil refineries and other energy facilities if Moscow also stopped its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's General Staff said on October 1 that Russian personnel losses hit an estimated 46,230 in September, the highest monthly figure of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces suffered an estimated 46,230 personnel losses in September, the highest monthly figure recorded by Ukraine so far in 2026, Ukraine's General Staff said on Oct. 1.

stories.headline: SpaceX Crew-13 reaches ISS in 7h55m, fastest trip ever by a US spacecraft

key_facts.fact: Crew-13 launched on a Falcon 9 at 11:10 a.m. EDT on October 1 from Cape Canaveral with NASA's Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA's Joshua Kutryk and Roscosmos' Sergey Teteryatnikov.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov arrived at the International Space Station at 7:05 p.m. EDT

key_facts.fact: Dragon 'Grace' docked at 7:05 p.m. EDT, 7 hours 55 minutes after launch, the fastest launch-to-docking of a US spacecraft in ISS history.
key_facts.excerpt: At 7-hours and 55-minutes, this marked the fastest launch-to-docking of a U.S. spacecraft in the history of the International Space Station.

key_facts.fact: The previous US record was 12h33m (cargo CRS-31, Nov 2024); the fastest crewed US trip had been 14h43m (Crew-11, Aug 2025). A Soyuz still holds the overall record at 3h03m.
key_facts.excerpt: The previous record was 12 hours and 33 minutes, set in November 2024 by SpaceX's Dragon cargo capsule during the robotic CRS-31 resupply flight. The fastest that astronauts had made the trip in a U.S. vehicle was 14 hours and 43 minutes ... In May 2020, a Russian Soyuz ... just 3 hours and 3 minutes

key_facts.fact: Watkins became the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit; the crew will stay about six months.
key_facts.excerpt: Watkins, the Crew-13's commander, became the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit. The crew is slated to stay at the ISS for six months

key_facts.fact: The launch had slipped from mid-September to replace a leaking valve in Dragon's propulsion system; Crew-12 is set to undock October 5 and splash down October 6.
key_facts.excerpt: The launch originally was planned for mid September, but the flight was delayed to replace a leaking valve in the Crew Dragon's propulsion system. ... Undocking is planned for Oct. 5 with splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the southern California coast on Oct. 6.

stories.headline: FDA approves first heart valve designed to be expanded as children grow

key_facts.fact: On October 1, the FDA approved the Autus Size-Adjustable Valve, a surgically implanted pulmonary valve for pediatric patients with congenital pulmonary valve disease.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved the Autus Size-Adjustable Valve, a surgically implanted pulmonary heart valve for pediatric patients with congenital pulmonary valve disease.

key_facts.fact: It is the first heart valve designed to be expanded after surgery to keep pace with a child's growth, and the first US-approved valve with polymeric rather than animal-tissue leaflets.
key_facts.excerpt: The Autus Size-Adjustable Valve is the first heart valve designed to be expanded after surgery to keep pace with a child's growth, and the first valve approved in the U.S. to use polymeric material ... than animal-derived tissue for its inner flaps

key_facts.fact: Expansion is done via a minimally invasive transcatheter procedure, potentially reducing repeat open-heart surgeries.
key_facts.excerpt: Valve expansion is performed through a minimally invasive transcatheter procedure, potentially reducing the need for repeat open-heart surgeries.

key_facts.fact: Edwards Lifesciences received the approval for the valve, developed by Autus Valve Technologies.
key_facts.excerpt: Edwards Lifesciences received approval for the Autus Size-Adjustable Valve, developed by Autus Valve Technologies Inc.

key_facts.fact: In the pivotal study, 100% of patients were free of device-related complications through 30 days, with no valve reinterventions through six months; patients will be followed for 10 years.
key_facts.excerpt: 100% of patients free from device-related complications through 30 days and demonstrating favorable valve performance with no AUTUS valve reinterventions through six months. ... Patients will continue to be followed for 10 years.

sources.title: FDA Approves First Heart Valve Designed to Grow with Children
Edwards Lifesciences Receives FDA Approval for AUTUS Valve, the First Surgical Pulmonary Valve for Pediatric Patients
